findings.assumption: Bullet 1 lets a dash right after the gate end it ("a dash follows it"); the argument rule covers only a separate next word.
findings.summary: The fix dropped the lookahead after an em or en dash (`\s?[—–]`), so a dash glued to an argument now names the gate: "Check: pnpm test —run passes.", "pnpm test –run" and "pnpm test—tests/a.test.ts" each return true (false in round 1). Smart-dash editors turn "--run" into "—run". This is a false gap, the cheaper error under the spec's cost rule, so it does not block. A fix: after an unspaced dash, require a letters-only word that a stop closes, as for a plain word (receipt review-27-r2-hunt-names.log).

findings.assumption: A word with an apostrophe or an inner dot is not "a plain word (letters only)" in bullet 1, so the spec does not require a match.
findings.summary: The new stop rule (punctuation must be followed by whitespace) also stops prose words: "Check: pnpm verify doesn't fail.", "pnpm verify isn't red." and "pnpm verify e.g. on CI." were gaps in round 1 and are now missed. Misses in every version: "pnpm test (the full suite) passes.", "pnpm test → all green.", "pnpm test & read the log.", "won’t" (curly apostrophe), "re-runs" and "run pnpm verify 2 times". The spec says a missed gate costs more than a false gap. A fix: let a plain word take an apostrophe tail (`\p{L}+(?:['’]\p{L}+)?`) and let `(` or an arrow end the gate (receipt review-27-r2-hunt-names.log).

findings.assumption: The coordinator rule stands: any non-symlink file in a feature or archive folder counts as a record.
findings.summary: Judged risk of the accepted rule: real for some stacks, not all. go test ./... compiles every package, so any .go file in a feature folder (a test or a plain probe.go) joins the gate run: a red x_test.go and a broken probe.go each fail go test ./... while the old receipt still pushes. pytest with no testpaths collects test_*.py and conftest.py under docs/features (1 failed). Vitest and Jest default includes (**/*.test.*, **/*.spec.*) would collect x.test.ts the same way. pytest with testpaths, cargo test, Maven (src/test only) and RSpec (spec/**) do not. Reviewers in this repo already write runnable probes into receipts (docs/features/2026-11-21-drift-tidy/reviews/receipts/spec-04-probe.mjs and others). Narrowing records to non-source extensions (.md, .json, .log, .txt, .diff, .patch) would keep every session-end record and receipt and close this (receipt review-27-r2-hunt-docs.log).

findings.assumption: Bullet 14 exempts the docs root by design; Markdown and JSON are the narrowed form.
findings.summary: Markdown and JSON elsewhere under the docs root still push on an old receipt when a build or test reads them: docs/package.json (a docs workspace package that pnpm -r test runs), docs/tsconfig.json, and Markdown that doctests read (pytest --doctest-glob, Rust include_str! doc tests). The spec decides this, so it is a note for the owner only. Excluding package.json and tsconfig*.json under the docs root would close the manifest case.
